actions.operation: Create an all-around supporting structure that forms a step at the bottom of the frame by offsetting the inner wall.

steps: Establish the requested through-thickness orientation from the asymmetric edge treatment rather than from a camera label: F007, represented by FACE 35 through FACE 42, is the continuous 10 mm outer fillet and therefore identifies the user-defined top side. F009 and FACE 34 are the adjacent narrow top land. The opposite broad planar land F008, FACE 12, is consequently the bottom working side.

Use FACE 12 as the support sketch plane, or construct a datum plane coincident with FACE 12 if direct face sketching is undesirable. Set the extrusion direction normal to FACE 12 and away from the existing frame, opposite the F007/F009 top side.

Project the complete rounded-rectangular inner perimeter associated with F002 onto the sketch. The source inner-wall geometry consists of straight wall faces FACE 9, FACE 11, FACE 33, and FACE 45 and 50 mm-radius corner wall faces FACE 8, FACE 10, FACE 46, and FACE 47.

Offset the projected inner contour inward into the central opening by 20 mm. This direction reduces the clear opening and enlarges the bottom seating area. Preserve a continuous closed rounded-rectangular contour through all four corners.

Create the supporting profile as a closed annular region whose inner boundary is the new 20 mm inward offset and whose outer boundary overlaps or follows the existing bottom frame land sufficiently to produce a robust union. Prefer using the outer wire of FACE 12 so the new base supports the complete existing frame land while extending 20 mm into the opening.
Pad or extrude the support profile 5 mm from FACE 12 away from the original body. Use an additive union so the support becomes part of SOLID 0 and remains continuous around the entire opening.

Verify that the resulting feature forms one valid solid, creates a uniform 5 mm-high bottom step, and retains a continuous reduced central opening without self-intersections at the 50 mm-radius corners.

actions.target: The top-side transition edges associated with the newly created supporting structure.
actions.relational_constraint: Apply the radii from the top to produce a smooth transition from above; do not apply them to the bottom edges.

steps: Perform this fillet after the support extrusion and Boolean union so the new transition-edge loop exists in the final topology.
Select the continuous upper inner edge loop of the support: the loop where the exposed top surface of the inward-projecting support meets its new inner vertical wall around the reduced opening.

Use F002 inner-wall faces FACE 8, FACE 9, FACE 10, FACE 11, FACE 33, FACE 45, FACE 46, and FACE 47 and bottom land FACE 12 as localization references. The selected edges themselves are newly generated and therefore do not have original-model B-rep IDs.
Apply a constant-radius 2 mm fillet to the complete upper transition loop, propagating through all straight and rounded-corner segments.

Confirm that the fillet is applied only from the upper side of the support and produces a smooth approach into the reduced opening. Do not include the lower inner edge or any edge belonging to the final bottom face.
Check that the 2 mm radius is compatible with the 5 mm support thickness and the 20 mm flange width and that no corner segment fails or collapses.

actions.target: The bottom face of the frame and supporting structure.
actions.relational_constraint: The bottom must remain flat and must not be altered by the top fillets.

Restrict the 2 mm fillet operation to the upper transition loop and verify that no selected fillet edge is incident to the terminal bottom face.
Do not add draft, chamfer, crown, recess, or lower-edge rounding to the support base.

Validate the completed geometry by checking that all points on the final bottom face or coplanar face set share one plane, that the enlarged seating area is continuous around the opening, and that the result remains a single valid solid.
